cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no gate in continuous integration to prevent regressions from reaching production. Comparable production systems at this stage of maturity typically maintain 40 to 60% coverage. This gap means defects in untested code paths have no automated detection before deployment.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are otherwise performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: Production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented access-handover process, and that engineer works on a rolling month-to-month contract. If the engineer departs without notice—the contract terms permit this—the company loses access to its production database until credentials can be rotated, a process that will require either restoring from backups or emergency vendor support. There is no compensating control. This is a critical risk to availability.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy or process for handling data-subject deletion requests. This means the company cannot demonstrate compliance with retention limits under GDPR, CCPA, and similar regimes, nor can it fulfill deletion rights when exercised. There is no compensating control. A regulator can require immediate purge of all historical data and assess penalties retroactively.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage across the codebase sits at 31%, with no coverage gate enforced in continuous integration. The three most recent production incidents each originated in untested edge cases. Deployments are performed manually, and there is no documented rollback procedure to contain the blast radius if a deployment fails. The combination of low coverage, no gating mechanism, and manual deployment creates a direct path for regressions to reach customers.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table, readable to any operator with database access. This means an employee with legitimate access to the database can view every customer password without restriction or audit trail, and a data breach exposes them all at once without the protection of cryptographic hashing. We strongly recommend moving to an industry-standard password hashing algorithm such as bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2 immediately, with a migration path for existing passwords on next login.

Deployments are performed manually with no documented rollback procedure and no automation to recover a failed production release. The most recent incident, 6 months ago, required 2 hours to restore the previous version, and the team cannot reliably repeat the steps. This creates a window where an erroneous deployment stands unchallenged, with recovery dependent on available engineering staff and institutional memory rather than a tested process.

Code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a documented convention. Some modules carry inline annotations on most functions; others have none. This has no bearing on application correctness or security at the company's current scale, but becomes a friction point as the team grows and the cost of onboarding rises.
